entries.title: Core model stays renderer/runtime neutral
entries.notes: The production facade composes the renderer-neutral semantic, session, action, and runtime packages.

entries.title: State transitions occur through typed actions or explicit events
Actions expose stable IDs, schemas, validation, risk metadata, confirmation metadata, and typed results
Side effects stay in application-supplied ports with no hidden core I/O
State snapshots are serializable and versioned
Snapshot exposes role, accessible name, value, state, relations, visibility, focusability, and stable ref
Stable refs disambiguate duplicate labels inside one snapshot/action cycle
Invalidated refs emit remap or divergence information
Every meaningful human action has keyboard and typed machine equivalents
Agent control negotiates capabilities before action execution
Structured action errors carry stable codes and safe context
JSONL and/or JSON-RPC over stdio is available for non-interactive control
Coordinate or canvas fallback is explicit, negotiated, and lower priority than semantic interaction
Theme resolves the required semantic role groups
Primitives consume semantic roles rather than raw ramps or global theme state
Theme supports dark or light policy and capability overrides
Density is configurable without changing semantic structure
Motion is tokenized and reduced-motion policy disables timing dependence
Marks, icons, banners, and ASCII fallbacks are pluggable assets
Renderer accepts model, viewport, capabilities, theme, and event context explicitly
Plain-text renderer exists as the reference CI-safe output
Terminal renderer sanitizes untrusted control characters at the final write boundary
Primitive set includes the required foundational, collection, state, input, viewport, and frame primitives
Tables support sticky headers, numeric alignment, selection, and non-modal disclosure
Renderer supports deterministic narrow, no-colour, ASCII, and non-TTY degradation
Lopper integration lives outside core and preserves Lopper domain semantics
entries.notes: Lopper is the first proving client and owns its domain adapter in the Lopper repository; the proof reference is a portable external citation until the worktree is published. Stave core remains application-neutral.

entries.title: Lopper adapter preserves command grammar and codemod or baseline confirmation behavior
entries.notes: The typed command and confirmation integration exists in the unpublished Lopper proving-client worktree; GA evidence requires a published, immutable Lopper revision.

entries.title: Lopper adapter supports existing snapshot and non-interactive paths
entries.notes: The snapshot and non-interactive parity suite exists in the unpublished Lopper proving-client worktree; GA evidence requires a published, immutable Lopper revision.

entries.title: A contrasting non-Lopper fixture uses the core before compatibility claims
entries.notes: Atlas is a distinct second client and regression rig with its own Program, action registry, semantic actions, deterministic replay, brand, seven semantic scenarios, and nine capability profiles. Its checked-in 63-case matrix and the Lopper render trace prove distinct application shapes over the same core contracts.

entries.title: Lopper adoption
entries.notes: The opt-in Lopper proving-client integration, semantic parity harness, command/action preservation, snapshots, and rollback flag exist in the Lopper worktree; the proof references are portable external citations until the worktree is published. Atlas independently proves a second brand/client shape.

entries.title: Root public API contains no Bubble Tea, Lip Gloss, Bubbles, tcell, or Lopper type
Root dependency graph excludes Lopper and optional adapter dependencies
Themes produce visibly distinct output without changing primitives
Replacing a node changes generation and rejects stale actions
Same replay inputs produce identical revision, tree, and surface hashes
Reducer, view, layout, and headless render pass without a TTY
Every interactive primitive has accessible role, name, action, and focus semantics
Every human command has a typed machine equivalent
No-colour, ASCII, narrow, non-TTY, CI, reduced-motion, and accessible-line profiles retain complete meaning
Machine output contains no ANSI, banners, prompts, or progress decoration
Secret values do not appear in snapshots, protocol, logs, diagnostics, replay, or surfaces
Consequential actions require valid policy or confirmation and reject replay
Queue saturation is bounded and observable
Cancellation restores the terminal and prevents late mutation
Lopper Start or Snapshot flows, commands, TTY refresh, sanitization, baseline, and codemod safety stay covered
entries.notes: The Lopper parity and consequential-action coverage is present locally but remains unpublished and therefore cannot satisfy the GA gate.

entries.title: Lopper adapter imports Stave and Stave never imports Lopper
entries.notes: Stave's import boundary is proven locally; the reciprocal Lopper dependency proof requires a published Lopper revision and consumable Stave module version.

entries.title: Bubble Tea and Lip Gloss adapters pass the same semantic or surface fixtures
Formatting, vet, tests, race, fuzz smoke, vulnerability, licence, and benchmark gates pass fresh
